advisories.title: The frozen Codex v4 ACCEPT is the one predecessor verdict the rebuilt ledger does not pin
advisories.what: Six independent reviewer verdicts exist on disk across this lineage: Codex v1, Claude 2 v2, Claude 2 v3, Codex v3, Claude 2 v4 and Codex v4. The ledger pins five. Codex v4 - ACCEPT, 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories, frozen at mode 0444, digest 665c215e... matching the dispatch - has no entry and is named nowhere in the artifact.
advisories.whyIRaisedIt: The generation's whole purpose was to repair an incomplete predecessor-verdict inventory, and the omitted verdict belongs to the very generation v5 answers. Filesystem mtimes put the Codex v4 file 104 seconds before v5, so it was on disk and frozen when v5 was authored - this is not a could-not-have-known. v4 itself set the disclosure precedent: when Codex v3 was unfrozen at authoring, v4 booked that fact in notFoldedThisSuccessor. v5 books nothing. A coordinator reading only this ledger sees the v4 round drawing a REJECT and no other review, when in fact it drew one REJECT and one ACCEPT.
advisories.whyAdvisoryAndNotShouldFix: I tested this against the calibration this lineage has actually been applying rather than against how bad it sounds. My own v4 S-1 was a SHOULD-FIX on two prongs: digest-pinned records left the artifact, and a booked forward obligation became unexecutable. Neither prong is present here - nothing was deleted, because this entry was never there, and no line in the artifact names Codex v4 and so nothing is left dangling. The prong that governs is the one Codex v3 used to rate LQMCV3-A1 an advisory: no finding is concealed. Codex v4's finding set is empty, so a ledger named appliesFindingsOf omits exactly zero findings by leaving it out. Withholding ACCEPT over the absence of an entry with three empty arrays would be inventing a stricter bar at v5 than the bar I applied at v4.
advisories.suggestedNotRequired: A successor could pin codexv4 alongside claude2v4 for symmetry, or state the rotation rule - that zero-finding verdicts are recorded by the dispatch chain rather than by this ledger. Either closes it. Neither is needed for this candidate to stand.

advisories.what: The sole element of the not-folded list reads 'Claude v3 ADV-1 / CODEX-V3-A1: blockers [] restored on the restored codexv1 entry this generation.' The value states the item was folded; the key states it was not. v4's element was internally consistent - it read 'is not folded here.' v5 changed the value's meaning without moving it.
advisories.whyIRaisedIt: The same act is booked twice with opposite senses: honestyRepairsFromV4 records the blockers [] restoration as a completed repair, and notFoldedThisSuccessor records it as an outstanding carry. This lineage's live defect at v3 and v4 was precisely an artifact holding two incompatible answers to one question, so the shape is worth naming even where the stakes are low.

The value text is accurate and self-correcting on its own line, the repair log states the same truth in the right sense, and codexv1.blockers == [] is verifiably present in the bytes, so all three sources agree on the fact and disagree only on the shelf it is filed under. A reader cannot be misled past the end of the sentence.

advisories.title: idCollisionNote discloses three of the five reviewer-id renamings, and the undisclosed pair is where the real collision lives
advisories.what: Measured against the frozen reviewer files, the ledger renames every id it records. Codex v1's true ids are LQMCV1-S1, LQMCV1-A1 and LQMCV1-A2; the ledger writes CODEX-V1-S1/A1/A2. Claude 2 v2's true id is S-1; the ledger writes CLAUDE-V2-S1. idCollisionNote declares the mapping for Codex v3 (LQMCV3-* to CODEX-V3-*), Claude v3 (ADV-1) and Claude v4 (S-1 to CLAUDE-V4-S1), but says nothing about Codex v1 or Claude v2.
advisories.whyIRaisedIt: The undisclosed pair is where the note is most load-bearing. Claude v2 and Claude v4 both genuinely used the bare id S-1 - that is an actual collision between two entries in this same ledger, and the note resolves only the later one. A field that exists to manage id collisions should name the collision it actually has.
advisories.whyAdvisoryAndNotShouldFix: The renaming is systematic, predictable from the generation prefix, and one hop from proof: every entry pins the reviewer file's digest, so the true ids are recoverable by opening the pinned bytes. No finding count is misstated - I parsed all five pinned files and each recorded verdict, blocker count, SHOULD-FIX count and advisory count matches its source exactly. The substance is inherited from v2/v3 rather than introduced here, though v5 did rewrite this field and had the opening to complete it.
advisories.suggestedNotRequired: Extend the note with the Codex v1 and Claude v2 mappings.

advisories.title: The D-056 citation attaches a temporal condition D-056 does not record
advisories.what: Three times the artifact says D-056 listed DR-118 ineligible for Class B SATISFIED 'while thresholds remain design-undecided' or 'while per-row thresholds remain design-undecided.' D-056's text is unconditional: 'DR-103/104/105/114/118 and the twelve no-contract rows remain ineligible.' It gives no per-row reason and sets no expiry. The reason is the artifact's own inference, presented as D-056's.
advisories.whyIRaisedIt: The 'while' reads as a lapse condition - decide the thresholds and the ineligibility ends. D-056 does not work that way: eligibility requires all five gates, and DR-118 sits on a flat ineligible list. A successor could mistake this for a standing promise that threshold closure alone converts DR-118 to Class-B-eligible. That is the prose-settles-what-it-may-not-settle family this lineage guards against elsewhere, in goldenClasses and matrixShape.
advisories.whyAdvisoryAndNotShouldFix: The inference is sound on the merits - D-056's second gate requires the remainder be 'only execution / measurement', and DR-118's remainder is an undecided design question, so it fails that gate for the stated reason. And the direction of error is strictly conservative: every one of the three sentences is deployed to deny SATISFIED, never to claim eligibility. The artifact nowhere asserts that DR-118 becomes eligible on threshold closure. An over-attributed rationale that only ever argues against its own author's interest does not warrant withholding acceptance.
advisories.suggestedNotRequired: Attribute the list to D-056 and the rationale to the artifact - D-056 lists DR-118 ineligible; the gate it fails is the execution/measurement-only gate.
